track.why: Jul 24 2024. Report describes the Goodell Creek forest climb, the notch above Terror Basin, the glacial lake outlet and slabs, the snow gully to the col and the class 3 scramble to the summit: our West Ridge route step by step. The track is a round trip from the trailhead, summit within 4 m. It starts about 460 m from our trailhead pin, so the pin is a little off but a confirmed coordinate could not be found.

facts.text: A bees nest sits under a large boulder beside the forest climb at about 4,800-4,900 ft; in late July a party was swarmed there.
In late July a stream was still running at roughly 5,200-5,300 ft, so top up there before the drop into the basin.
Rangers patrol the basin in summer checking permits, food storage and human-waste bags, so have all three sorted.
Around July 1-2 the snow was negligible up to the notch, but a short cornice remnant at the col had to be downclimbed, and the basin snow was firm enough in the morning for crampons.
By late August the snow finger has shrunk to a short strip and its last stretch is bare, very loose rock; keep partners out of each other's fall line.
In late August mornings the outlet boulders of the glacial lake can be glazed with ice, making the crossing slick.
From early August on, several parties skipped the snow finger because of constant rockfall and scrambled loose rock to its right.
Cairns between the basin camp and the glacier base lead nowhere in places; navigate the dark section by map, not cairns.
Descending from the lake outlet back to camp, a lower line along cairns ended in a cliff band that forced a re-ascent; stay on the rocky benches used on the way up.

notes: West Ridge tracks 3319995, 2585301, 995369 all start about 460 m from our Goodell Creek trailhead pin (48.68664,-121.27121); the recordings cluster near 48.6827,-121.2692. Search found no mapped coordinate for the Upper Goodell Group Camp trailhead (a WTA guidebook list gives 48.6733,-121.2658 unlabelled), so no pin move is proposed.
